---
title: "Maintaining the documentation"
---

The site is built with [Great Docs](https://posit-dev.github.io/great-docs/) and Quarto. Narrative pages live in the
directories under `docs/`; `docs/index.qmd` is the homepage. The root `index.qmd` is a symbolic link that lets Great
Docs find it (since it requires the index in the repo root). The root `great-docs.yml` configures branding and navigation.
Python API reference generation is disabled because ToFScope's internal modules are not intended as a public library interface.

## Building and previewing

From the repository root, the following commands install the regular dependencies together with the documentation
group and build the site:

```sh
uv sync --group docs
uv run great-docs build
```

For rapid editing, the local preview script watches documentation sources, rebuilds the site automatically,
and refreshes the browser after a successful build:

```sh
uv run scripts/preview_docs.py
```

The docs preview should open at `http://127.0.0.1:3000/`. The `--port` option selects another port,
and `--no-browser` starts the server without opening a tab. Pressing **Ctrl-C** stops the preview.
If a build fails, the script reports the error and waits for the next source change.

For a static preview of an existing build, `uv run --group docs great-docs preview` remains available. After a build,
`python scripts/check_docs.py great-docs/_site` can be used to check local links, anchors, and image paths.

The pinned version of Great Docs (*0.17.0*) uses a root-level `great-docs.yml`. Its generated Quarto project
is `great-docs/`, with the deployable site in `great-docs/_site/`. The pre-render hook `scripts/prepare_docs.py`
copies shared images into that generated project and creates narrative `llms.txt` and `llms-full.txt` exports.
This fills a gap in that release when API reference generation is disabled.

## Editing a page

Section pages use `.qmd` files with a `title` in their YAML frontmatter. Numeric filename prefixes control order;
Great Docs removes them from published URLs. Links between guide pages use the original prefixed filename,
such as `30-architecture.qmd`; Great Docs rewrites those links during the build.

Diagrams use `{mermaid}` code fences. Rendered diagrams should be inspected in the browser in both light and
dark modes to ensure they look okay. Shared screenshots and logos live in `docs/assets/` and can be referenced
from guide pages with `../assets/` paths.

### Interactive screenshots

Some user-guide screenshots link explanatory text to a highlighted area of the image. The page places an image and
empty, uniquely identified `explore-highlight` spans inside an `explore-overview` container using a raw HTML block.
Each span's `left`, `top`, `width`, and `height` are percentages of the image container. A regular Markdown link to
the span's ID scrolls to that area; `docs/styles.css` uses `:target` to draw the highlight.

For example, a guide can use this pattern:

~~~~markdown
[Open the control](#example-control).

```{=html}
<div class="explore-overview">
  <img src="../assets/example.png" alt="Description of the interface.">
  <span id="example-control" class="explore-highlight" style="left:10%;top:20%;width:15%;height:5%" aria-hidden="true"></span>
</div>
```
~~~~

The numbered Explore overview in [Signals and views](../using-tofscope/10-signals-and-views.qmd) also overlays
`explore-marker` buttons on the image. These provide descriptions on hover or keyboard focus. Make sure to give
each button an accessible label and associate its tooltip with `aria-describedby`. When replacing an image,
update the percentage positions and check the links, highlights, and
tooltips at different viewport sizes and with keyboard navigation. Keep useful alt text and written instructions so the
guide does not depend on the image alone.

The source pages, assets, configuration, workflow, and dependency lockfile are committed to the repository.
Generated `great-docs/`, standalone HTML previews, and Quarto `*_files/` folders are ignored.

## Publishing

The Documentation workflow (`.github/workflows/docs.yml`) builds documentation previews on pull requests and builds and
deploys on merges or pushes to `main`. It uses the locked documentation dependencies and pinned Quarto version, and uploads
`great-docs/_site/` to GitHub Pages.

To activate publishing, a repository administrator must select **GitHub Actions** in
**Settings → Pages → Build and deployment → Source**. Once the workflow is merged and deployed, the site will be available
at <https://datasophos.github.io/ToFScope/>. Local builds do not change repository settings or publish the site.

### Pull request previews

The Git-connected Cloudflare Pages project `tofscope-docs` builds branch previews separately from the GitHub Pages
production site. These builds are controlled by the workflow in `.github/workflows/cloudflare-previews.yml`. Its root
directory is the repository root, build command is `sh scripts/build_cloudflare_docs.sh`, and
output directory is `great-docs/_site`. Its build variables are `PYTHON_VERSION=3.12` and `SKIP_DEPENDENCY_INSTALL=1`.
The script installs documentation dependencies, checks local links, and adds a `noindex` header. Automatic Cloudflare
production deployments are disabled; GitHub Pages remains the canonical production site.

Preview builds watch `docs/*`, `great-docs.yml`, `index.qmd`, the documentation build and checking scripts,
`pyproject.toml`, and `uv.lock`. Cloudflare evaluates these paths for each push, so a code-only push to an existing
documentation pull request does not refresh the preview. Cloudflare attaches preview URLs to pull requests from
branches in the same repository; it does not automatically create them for pull requests from forks.

Cloudflare posts its `pages.dev` preview links directly to pull requests. When a pull request closes, the cleanup
workflow requests deletion of its branch's preview deployments, unless another open pull request uses that branch.
It runs on pull request events and every 15 minutes to retry cleanup. Cloudflare documents restrictions on deleting
the latest branch deployment; check the workflow if deletion is rejected. Preview URLs remain available until their
deployments are deleted. They are public and return a `noindex` header.

The cleanup workflow uses trusted code from the default branch, never code from a pull request, and requires
the GitHub Actions repository secret `CLOUDFLARE_PREVIEW_TOKEN` with account **Pages Write** permission.
The Cloudflare account and project are defined in `scripts/cloudflare_previews.py`; update them there if
the hosting account changes. To troubleshoot, inspect the Pages deployment and the cleanup workflow separately.
The workflow becomes active after it is merged into the default branch.
